log.note: R412 baseline: the pin starts at the code-module digest of the main tip this change is cut from (INDEXER_VERSION 1)
A-037 deletes two functions of equivalence.py that nothing calls (ring_terms and candidate_languages; not index_article, not anything else); no row an article gets is written differently
R415 on the A-037 base: the www modules and gazetteers left the keyword digest and index_article gained the www stamp write; keyword rows are unchanged

store.py changed only in prune_orphan_keywords (R632: the epoch bump moved behind the day-count check) and its imports; index_article and every function it calls are untouched, so the rows an article gets are identical
R689: backfill_corpus only looks at a stop before each article; index_article and the rows it writes are unchanged
R689: backfill_corpus only looks at a stop before each article and before its closing counts; index_article and the rows it writes are unchanged

PR #1949 (audit P2/P8) replaced the quadratic comment, tag, style/script and e-mail regexes in extract.py, text_processor.py and markup_blocks.py with linear scans that are byte-identical to the old regexes (differential on every shipped HTML page, 300k seeded random documents incl. Unicode case folds, tests/test_html_strips_linear.py), so no row index_article writes can change

R699 causes 1, 3 and 4: an asserted language its text's own script refutes is cleared and re-deduced (keywords move to the right language and stoplist), and script-code lines and LaTeX command names are blanked before tokenising (no more addclass/mathcal keywords); R697: the pooled re-index now extracts dates under the article's own language (never the stoplist's "en" guess) and a tag stored with no language says so in its extractor field
R101 merged onto R699/R697: index_article skips a quarantined article's counter delta and reads its flag from idx_article_quarantined; the mention and date rows it writes are those of version 2

R698: a keyword row in one language never takes another language's mention (extraction, fold and restore carry); row 31: a re-extraction removes this extractor's unjudged candidate date tags it no longer finds and relabels the ones it finds again. Old rows converge only after a re-index.
Only a docstring in src/analytics/reindex_parallel.py changed (terminate_live_pools now describes the R689 shutdown order); no row index_article writes can change.
PR #1972: datestore.articles_for_date also returns each tag's id for the Agenda's confirm and reject, and sentiment.py gains a comment-only perf pointer; the rows index_article writes are unchanged

Scheduling only: the serial precompute computes when/where/who before the write gate (the same extraction, arguments and R697 language as the pool and the inline path), the re-index computes the next window while writing the current one, and the drain's workers and commit width change; the rows index_article writes are identical

Scheduling only: the serial precompute computes when/where/who before the write gate from the same text, extractors and arguments as the inline path (the raw content column for an article kept compressed, the anchor, country and R697 language), the re-index computes the next window while writing the current one, and the drain's workers and commit width change; the rows index_article writes are identical

The serial precompute no longer skips www for an article whose keyword half failed; the apply redoes that article inline whole, so the precomputed result is unused and the rows index_article writes are identical.

src/analytics/store.py gained catch_up_source_counters and a chunked scoped reconcile_source_counters (Source.article_count bookkeeping, row 75); no function index_article calls changed, so the rows an article gets are identical
R758 row 210: the engine identity hashes data file names in POSIX form and also accepts the pre-R758 Windows id of the same bytes; the rows index_article writes are unchanged

row 239: safe_yaml maps libyaml 0.2.6's own nesting error (PyYAML 6.0.4) to the same YAMLDepthError; a document that parsed before parses to the same value, and a refused one is refused as before, so the rows an article gets are identical

src/timemap/datestore.py changed only in its agenda READ path (upcoming_deduced gains a default limit, truncated and ids_complete; a new read-only deduced_date_article_ids); extract_dates and every function index_article calls to write date rows are untouched, so the rows an article gets are identical (row 399)
